marks.gloss_en: והתניא: ובלבד שיגביה מן הקרקע טפח -- the baraita states its handbreadth condition as one of height from the ground
כי תניא ההיא בחבלא דביני ביני -- that baraita speaks of the rope in between (= p_chavla_devenei_benei)
the baraita: provided he raises [the rope] a handbreadth from the ground
מאי משמע דהאי גימון לישנא דמיכף? דכתיב הלכף כאגמן ראשו -- from where is it implied that gimon is a term of bending? as it is written, 'to bow his head like an agmon'
and a calf may not go out with a gimon (the mishna's clause, cited)
a donkey does not go out with a saddlecloth when it is not tied to it
and roosters do not go out with strings
and ewes do not go out chanunot
what is the reason [the donkey may not go out with an untied saddlecloth]? -- as we have said [earlier]
כי הא דאמר רבי חנינא -- the elders are judged for not protesting against the princes
מאי דכתיב ה' במשפט יבא עם זקני עמו ושריו
Rav Pappa: and those of the Exilarch's house are apprehended for the whole world
וחדא פרה הויא ליה? והא אמר רב... תריסר אלפי עגלי הוה מעשר -- did he have only one cow? he tithed twelve thousand calves a year (memra-against-mishnah; kind svara for want of a construct)
the mishnah: the cow of R' Elazar ben Azarya [went out with a strap between its horns, against the Sages' will]

וחדא פרה הויא ליה? והא אמר רב... תריסר אלפי עגלי הוה מעשר מעדריה כל שתא ושתא -- did he have only one cow, that the mishna speaks of 'his cow'? (kind svara: no ObjectionKind for an amoraic-memra objection, והא אמר)
תנא: לא שלו היתה אלא של שכינתו, ומתוך שלא מיחה בה נקראת על שמו -- it was his neighbour's, called by his name because he did not protest (= p_shel_shchenato, p_nikreit_al_shmo)
the cow was not his; it was his neighbour's
(54b.19, next piska) תנא: לא שלו היתה אלא של שכינתו היתה, ומתוך שלא מיחה בה נקראת על שמו -- it was not his but his neighbour's, and because he did not protest it is called by his name
the stam: throughout Seder Moed, wherever this pair appears, take out R' Yochanan and put in R' Yonatan
nor [may] a cow [go out] with a hedgehog skin (the mishna's clause, cited)
בשלמא דרב הונא, היינו דקתני חנונות -- granted on Rav Huna's account: that is why [the mishna] teaches 'chanunot'
אלא לרבנן מאי חנונות -- but according to the Rabbanan [who do not say yachnun], what is [the sense of] 'chanunot'?
דעבדינן להו מילתא דמרחמינן עלייהו -- we do for them something by which we show them mercy (= p_chanunot_rachamim)
[they are called chanunot] because we do for them something by which we show them mercy
אמר ליה רב חסדא: אם כן עשיתה מר עוקבא -- if so, you have made it Mar Ukva
and ewes may not go out chanunot (the mishna's clause, cited)
אמר ליה רב נחמן: אם כן עשיתה ילתא -- if so, you have made it Yalta
Rav Pappa bar Shmuel: when it crouches to give birth, they soak two swatches of oil and place one on its forehead and one on the womb so that it will be warmed
אי הכי זכרים נמי -- if [the chip is to make the worms fall], rams too [should go out with it, yet the mishna names ewes]
כיון דמנגחי זכרים בהדדי ממילא נפלן -- since rams butt one another, [the worms] fall of themselves
Rav Huna: there is a tree in the coastal cities named yachnun; they bring a chip [of it] and place it in its nose
nor [may a cow go out] with the strap between its horns (the mishna's clause, cited)
that they make it for the gizra
nor [may roosters go out] with a strap (the mishna's clause, cited)
Rav Huna: [the 'ladder' on its neck is] a bei lo'a (a jaw-piece)
that they make them a sign, so that they will not be exchanged
because it looks like one going to the chinga (a fair/procession)
